types.name: Physical payload
types.desc: Data read from a disk, on its way to checksum verification.

types.name: I/O request
types.desc: zio_t moving through the pipeline, being retried, re-executed or completed.

types.name: Transaction
types.desc: dmu_tx_t assignment, or work done for one txg in syncing context.

types.name: Device I/O
types.desc: The block-device request and its completion status.

types.name: Control
types.desc: Calls and requests: counters, state changes, ioctls, status queries. Draw dashed.

types.name: Dirty time log
types.desc: Txg ranges a device is missing (DTL_MISSING / DTL_PARTIAL), in memory or as a space map.

types.name: Events
types.desc: Ereports, resource and sysevent nvlists in the zevent queue, zed agent events and fault lists.

contexts.name: Userspace: zpool and libzfs (also when called from zed)
Open context: the calling thread, inside a dmu_tx
Syncing context: txg_sync thread, one txg at a time
A dedicated kernel thread or delayed task (SPA async thread, deadman)
Runs in whichever context calls it
The userspace ZFS event daemon (zed) and its agent thread
Kernel, in the thread of the calling process (an ioctl on /dev/zfs, mount(2) or umount(2)) or a helper thread it starts, outside syncing context and outside any dmu_tx

groups.title: I/O pipeline (shared with the I/O graph)
groups.summary: Where a failed, wrong or slow I/O is noticed.

groups.title: Kernel records: counters, DTL, error log, suspend
groups.summary: What the kernel remembers about errors, and its own last-resort reactions.

groups.title: Ereports and the zevent queue
groups.summary: Events built in the kernel and queued for userspace readers.

groups.title: ZFS event daemon (zed)
groups.summary: Reads every event, runs zedlets and decides about faults and spares.

groups.title: libzfs and the zpool command
groups.summary: The userspace calls that read status and events and request state changes.

groups.title: Kernel vdev state changes
groups.summary: ioctls and the vdev code that faults, degrades, removes, onlines, clears and attaches spares.

groups.title: Transactions and sync context
groups.summary: What waits on a suspended pool, and what is written in each txg.

nodes.title: Data disks (normal class)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. The disk that misbehaves: it returns an error, returns wrong data without an error, answers late or not at all, or disappears.

nodes.title: Leaf vdev driver
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. On Linux, after a read or write that failed with EIO, vdev_disk_io_done() checks whether the block device is still there; if not, it asks for the vdev to be marked REMOVED.

nodes.title: I/O completion
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. The bio completion records the device's error in the zio and re-enters the pipeline on an interrupt taskq.

nodes.title: zio taskqs (issue / interrupt)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Runs completions, the single retry of a failed logical zio (at the head of the issue queue) and the re-execution of failed writes (on the claim issue taskq).

nodes.title: zio create + execute
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. zio_wait() is where a caller waits for an I/O; it triggers the deadman after zfs_deadman_ziotime_ms. Re-executed zios (after zpool clear) start here again.

nodes.title: VDEV_IO_START
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. For a leaf that is not accessible (dead, removal pending, or known unable to read or write) the zio fails at once with ENXIO and never reaches the disk.

nodes.title: VDEV_IO_DONE
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Lets the vdev type react (mirror: try another side; raidz: verify and reconstruct). An unexpected error on a leaf that still looks accessible starts a device probe.

nodes.title: VDEV_IO_ASSESS
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Only a logical zio is retried, once. A leaf error becomes ENXIO when the disk is no longer accessible, so it is blamed on the device rather than on the I/O.

nodes.title: CHECKSUM_VERIFY
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. A mismatch on a non-speculative read is counted against the leaf at once and a checksum ereport is started; the error is passed up so redundancy can supply another copy.

nodes.title: Mirror vdev
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. On a read error or bad checksum it reads the next child and then rewrites the children that failed. A write to a mirror counts as successful when at least one child succeeded (extra DVA copies all have to succeed).

nodes.title: RAIDZ / dRAID vdev
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. When the block does not verify, parity reconstruction finds which column was wrong; that child disk gets the checksum count and an ereport carrying both the good and the bad data, and the column is rewritten.

nodes.title: DONE
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. The main bookkeeping point: per-vdev statistics, slow I/O detection, io ereports and error counters for leaves, the error log and data ereport for failed logical zios, finishing checksum reports, and the decision to re-execute or to suspend the pool.

nodes.title: Per-vdev counters (vdev_stat_t)
nodes.role: In-memory statistics of each vdev: operations, bytes, latency histograms, repaired bytes, and the error counters vs_read_errors, vs_write_errors, vs_checksum_errors and vs_slow_ios that zpool status shows as READ, WRITE, CKSUM and SLOW. They are not stored on disk, start at zero when the pool is imported, are zeroed by zpool clear and when a disk is marked REMOVED. vdev_stat_update() also records failed writes in the DTL.

nodes.title: Dirty time logs (DTL)

ref.code: vdev_dtl_dirty(vdev_t *vd, vdev_dtl_type_t t, uint64_t txg, uint64_t size)
vdev_dtl_contains(vdev_t *vd, vdev_dtl_type_t t, uint64_t txg, uint64_t size)

nodes.role: Per-vdev range trees of txgs whose writes a device missed. A leaf's DTL_MISSING is persisted as a space map in syncing context; parents' DTLs are derived from their children. Used to skip reads from a disk that lacks the data, to decide whether a disk holds the only copy (vdev_dtl_required()), and to bound a resilver.

nodes.title: Persistent error log

ref.code: spa_log_error(spa_t *spa, const zbookmark_phys_t *zb, const uint64_t birth)

nodes.role: Bookmarks (objset, object, level, blkid; with the head_errlog feature also the birth txg, per head dataset) of logical blocks that failed. New entries collect in memory (spa_errlist_last, or spa_errlist_scrub while a scrub runs) and are written to ZAP objects in the MOS by spa_errlog_sync(). There are two on-disk logs, last and scrub; when a scan ends the scrub log replaces the last log.

nodes.title: Device probe
nodes.role: Reads, and if the pool is writable rewrites, the pad areas of labels 1 to 3 of a leaf. Only one probe per disk runs at a time; other zios that want one wait for it. If the disk cannot be both read and (on a writable pool) written, it is marked unable to read or write, a probe_failure ereport is posted and, for probes started by the pipeline, the kernel asks for the disk to be faulted.

nodes.title: Deadman (hung I/O detector)
nodes.role: Finds I/O that never completes. spa_deadman() runs when a txg sync lasts longer than zfs_deadman_synctime_ms and repeats every zfs_deadman_checktime_ms; vdev_deadman() then looks at the oldest active zio of every leaf. zio_wait() calls zio_deadman() for a waiter older than zfs_deadman_ziotime_ms. It logs and posts deadman ereports; zfs_deadman_failmode (wait, continue, panic) decides what else happens. Nothing is done while the pool is suspended.

nodes.title: Pool suspend / resume
nodes.role: zio_suspend() panics if failmode=panic; otherwise it logs a warning, posts an io_failure ereport, marks the pool suspended and parks the failed root zio under a "godfather" zio. New transactions then wait or fail depending on failmode. zio_resume() (from zpool clear) clears the state, wakes waiters and re-executes every parked zio from the start.

nodes.title: Ereport admission (zfs_ereport_post)
nodes.role: Every ereport passes three checks. Valid: not during tryimport or recovery, only read and write zios, not for a disk already known inaccessible, not a checksum error in a range the disk is known to be missing. Not a duplicate: an io or checksum ereport for a vdev and zio with the same pool, vdev, error, priority, offset, size and bookmark as one seen within zfs_zevent_retain_expire_secs is dropped (EALREADY); data ereports name no vdev and are never treated as duplicates. Not rate limited: delay, deadman and checksum ereports are limited per disk per second; dropped events are added to the readers' dropped count. zfs_ereport_clear() forgets the duplicate history (zpool clear, completed scrub). Delay ereports are only posted while the vdev property slow_io_events is on.

nodes.title: Ereport payload (zfs_ereport_start)
nodes.role: Builds the nvlist: class ereport.fs.zfs. followed by the subclass (io, checksum, data, delay, deadman, probe_failure, io_failure, vdev.open_failed and the other vdev.* classes ...), an ENA shared by all ereports of one logical I/O, a detector naming pool and vdev, and the payload: pool name, state and failmode; vdev guid, type, path, devid, the vdev's error counters and the spares; zio error, flags, stage, priority, offset, size, delay; the bookmark. For checksum, io and delay ereports it adds the vdev's checksum_n / checksum_t, io_n / io_t or slow_io_n / slow_io_t when they differ from the default, which is how zed learns per-disk SERD thresholds.

nodes.title: Checksum ereport (start / finish)
nodes.role: Checksum ereports carry a description of the damage, which needs the good data. For a mirror or single disk the ereport and a copy of the bad data are attached to the logical zio and finished when it completes; RAIDZ already has both buffers and posts at once. annotate_ecksum() records the bad byte ranges and how many bits were set and cleared.

nodes.title: Resource and sysevent posts

ref.code: zfs_event_create(spa_t *spa, vdev_t *vd, const char *type, const char *name,

nodes.role: Events that are not errors: resource.fs.zfs.statechange (a leaf changed state), resource.fs.zfs.removed, resource.fs.zfs.autoreplace, and sysevent.fs.zfs.* notices such as vdev_spare, vdev_attach, vdev_clear, resilver_finish and scrub_finish. Each carries pool and vdev guid, path and state.

nodes.title: zevent queue
nodes.role: One in-kernel list of events for all pools. zfs_zevent_post() adds a time and an event id (eid), inserts at the head and wakes waiting readers; when the list holds zfs_zevent_len_max events the oldest is dropped and every reader positioned on it is told how many it missed. Each open /dev/zfs file has its own cursor, so zed and zpool events read independently.

nodes.title: Event ioctls (/dev/zfs)
nodes.role: ZFS_IOC_EVENTS_NEXT returns the next event after the caller's cursor and the dropped count, and blocks until one arrives unless the caller asked not to. SEEK repositions the cursor (zed uses it to start over when its last processed eid is no longer in the queue); CLEAR empties the queue (zpool events -c).

nodes.title: Disk monitor (udev)
nodes.role: A zed thread listening to udev. Disk and partition add and remove uevents (including multipath and scsi_debug special cases) become EC_dev_add / EC_dev_remove events for the agents. They never pass through the kernel zevent queue.

nodes.title: zed event loop

ref.code: zed_event_seek(struct zed_conf *zcp, uint64_t saved_eid, int64_t saved_etime[])

nodes.role: Opens /dev/zfs, skips the events up to the last one it processed (eid and time kept in a state file), then reads events one at a time. Each event goes first to the agents, then to the zedlets, then its eid is saved. When the kernel reports dropped events it doubles zfs_zevent_len_max.

nodes.title: Zedlets (scripts)

ref.code: zed_exec_process(uint64_t eid, const char *class, const char *subclass,

nodes.role: Executables in the zedlet directory whose names start with the event class, the subclass or "all", run with the event as ZEVENT_* environment variables: notifications (statechange-notify.sh, data-notify.sh, scrub_finish-notify.sh), enclosure LEDs and slot power (statechange-sync-led.sh, deadman-sync-slot_off.sh), and others. Zedlets whose name continues the event name with "-sync-" wait for the zedlets started before them and finish before later ones start; the others run in parallel. They report; the fault decisions are made by the agents.

nodes.title: Agent dispatcher
nodes.role: A queue and one thread that hand each event to the agents subscribed to its class. Agents can post events to it too (the diagnosis engine's fault lists). A udev disk-remove event is rewritten here into resource.fs.zfs.removed.

nodes.title: Diagnosis engine (zfs-diagnosis)
nodes.role: Keeps one case per disk. Ignores ereports from before the pool was loaded, during import, io and checksum ereports during pool open, ereports for vdevs other than disks and files, and checksum ereports from scrub or resilver I/O. io and checksum ereports feed SERD engines; when one fires (and no other disk under the same parent has an active case) it solves the case: checksum and slow_io at once, io after a 15 second wait for a removal event. A removal resets the engines; a statechange to HEALTHY closes the case. A pool io_failure ereport is turned into a pool fault directly.

nodes.title: SERD engines

ref.code: fmd_serd_create(fmd_hdl_t *hdl, const char *name, uint_t n, hrtime_t t)

nodes.role: Soft Error Rate Discrimination: an engine remembers the times of its last N events and fires when N of them fall within T. Defaults: 10 io or checksum events within 600 seconds. A slow_io engine exists only when the disk has both slow_io_n and slow_io_t set. Once fired, an engine ignores events until it is reset.

nodes.title: Fault cases (list.suspect)
nodes.role: zed's small implementation of the illumos fault manager API. Solving a case builds a fault (fault.fs.zfs.vdev.io, vdev.checksum, vdev.slow_io, io_failure_wait / _continue, ...), logs it with its ZFS-8000 message code and posts a list.suspect event back to the agent queue.

nodes.title: Retire agent (zfs-retire)
nodes.role: Acts on fault lists: fault.fs.zfs.vdev.io faults the disk, vdev.checksum and vdev.slow_io degrade it, both with aux "too many errors", then it tries to attach a hot spare. On resource.fs.zfs.removed it requests removal if the kernel has not marked the disk REMOVED yet; on that event or a statechange to REMOVED or FAULTED it attaches a spare when spare_on_remove is set (default on). Spares are tried in order of preference (same rotational type, size, ...) until one attaches.

nodes.title: Hotplug agent (zfs_mod)
nodes.role: Handles disk-add events and the vdev_check sysevent (a device failed to open at import while autoreplace is on). It looks for a pool vdev with the same devid, physical path, guid or by-vdev path, skips healthy and plainly offlined ones, and onlines it; if that fails and the pool has autoreplace=on and the vdev was a whole disk in a bad state, it labels the new disk and replaces the old one with it. Without autoreplace it onlines again with ZFS_ONLINE_FORCEFAULT so that the failure is reported.

nodes.title: Administrator
nodes.role: The person or script typing the command. Every path in this graph that a command starts begins with a wire from this node; the arrows that come back into a command node are its results, errors and refusals.

nodes.title: zpool status / events / clear
nodes.role: The administrator's view. zpool status prints each vdev's state and READ, WRITE, CKSUM (and with -s SLOW) counts and "errors: N data errors"; with -v the affected files. zpool events prints the queued events; zpool clear clears errors and resumes a suspended pool.

nodes.title: libzfs event reader
nodes.role: Wraps ZFS_IOC_EVENTS_NEXT on a caller-supplied /dev/zfs file descriptor, growing the buffer when an event does not fit. Used by zed and by zpool events.

nodes.title: libzfs status readers
nodes.role: Fetches the pool configuration with statistics (ZFS_IOC_POOL_STATS) and the error log as an array of bookmarks (ZFS_IOC_ERROR_LOG), and turns dataset and object numbers into path names for display.

nodes.title: libzfs vdev state calls
nodes.role: Thin wrappers that send ZFS_IOC_VDEV_SET_STATE (faulted, degraded, online, removed) or ZFS_IOC_CLEAR. Used by zed's agents and by zpool online, offline -f and clear.

nodes.title: libzfs replace / spare attach
nodes.role: zpool attach and zpool replace, and the agents' spare activation and autoreplace: sends ZFS_IOC_VDEV_ATTACH with the new device and the replacing flag.

nodes.title: Status ioctls
nodes.role: Returns the pool configuration with each vdev's vdev_stat_t, the approximate error count and the suspended flag, and copies the error log out as bookmarks.

nodes.title: Vdev change ioctls
nodes.role: Dispatches a requested state (online, offline, faulted, degraded, removed) to the vdev code, and attach / replace requests to spa_vdev_attach(). A fault or degrade with an unknown aux reason is treated as "too many errors".

nodes.title: zfs_ioc_clear()
nodes.role: zpool clear: optionally rewinds a pool that failed to open, refuses to resume when multihost sees another host, clears the vdev errors under the vdev state lock and resumes suspended I/O. It does not touch the error log.

nodes.title: vdev_fault() / vdev_degrade()
nodes.role: Fault: the leaf is closed and gets no more I/O. The flag is written to the config, but when the pool is opened or imported again only a persistent forced fault (zpool offline -f, aux "external") is kept; a fault requested by zed is dropped and the disk is tried again. If the disk holds the only copy of some data it is reopened and left DEGRADED instead. Degrade: only a flag for the administrator; I/O continues normally. Only leaf vdevs can be faulted or degraded.

nodes.title: vdev_online() / vdev_remove_wanted()

ref.code: vdev_online(spa_t *spa, uint64_t guid, uint64_t flags, vdev_state_t *newstate)

nodes.role: Online clears the offline flags and reopens the top-level vdev; with ZFS_ONLINE_UNSPARE a spare attached in its place is detached after the resilver. Remove-wanted first probes the disk and refuses (EEXIST) if it still answers, then lets the async thread mark it REMOVED.

nodes.title: vdev_clear()
nodes.role: Zeroes the error counters of a vdev and all its children. A faulted, degraded or unreachable vdev gets its flags cleared and is reopened; a still-broken disk fails to open and, because vdev_forcefault is set, its ereport is posted again. Also forgets the vdev's duplicate-ereport history.

nodes.title: vdev_set_state()

ref.code: vdev_set_state(vdev_t *vd, boolean_t isopen, vdev_state_t state, vdev_aux_t aux)

nodes.role: Sets a vdev's state and aux reason, closes a leaf that is now dead, posts a statechange event for a leaf (and an ereport.fs.zfs.vdev.* ereport such as vdev.open_failed when it cannot be opened), and propagates upwards: a mirror or raidz with some unhealthy children becomes DEGRADED, with too many it can no longer be opened.

nodes.title: vdev_open() / vdev_reopen()
nodes.role: Closes and reopens a vdev tree. A faulted or offline leaf stays so; a missing one stays REMOVED; otherwise it becomes HEALTHY or DEGRADED. A leaf that opened successfully is checked for a needed resilver.

nodes.title: SPA async thread
nodes.role: Work that cannot be done in the I/O completion path: marking vdevs REMOVED (counters zeroed, removed event posted), faulting vdevs whose probe failed (DEGRADED and pool suspend instead when the disk holds the only copy), starting a resilver, detaching finished replacements and spares.

nodes.title: spa_vdev_attach()

ref.code: spa_vdev_attach(spa_t *spa, uint64_t guid, nvlist_t *nvroot, int replacing,

nodes.role: Inserts a spare vdev (for a hot spare) or a replacing vdev above the old disk, adds the new disk with a DTL covering every txg, marks a hot spare active, posts vdev_spare and vdev_attach events and starts a resilver (or a sequential rebuild for a dRAID spare, or defers it while another resilver runs).

nodes.title: Resilver trigger
nodes.role: Decides whether a reopened leaf needs a resilver (its DTL is not empty) and asks the async thread to start one, unless a running resilver already covers its txgs; with resilver_defer a newer gap is deferred instead of restarting. dsl_scan_restart_resilver() starts the scan, which continues in the scrub and resilver graph.

nodes.title: dmu_tx (transaction)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Every change starts by assigning a transaction. On a suspended pool the assignment fails with ESHUTDOWN. dmu_tx_assign() turns that into EIO when failmode=continue (unless the caller passed DMU_TX_SUSPEND), otherwise into a retry, so a caller that waits blocks until the pool resumes.

nodes.title: spa_sync()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Each txg: arms the deadman, writes the pending error-log entries, runs the scan (which may finish a scrub or resilver), writes dirty DTLs through vdev_sync(), and finally rewrites the labels and uberblocks.

nodes.title: Uberblock + label update
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. If writing the labels and uberblocks fails (vdev_config_sync() returns an error), the txg cannot be committed: the pool suspends and spa_sync() waits for zpool clear, then tries again.

nodes.title: dsl_scan_done()
nodes.role: The end of a scrub or resilver: DTLs are reassessed, the error log is rotated (scrub log becomes last log, also when the scan was cancelled), the duplicate-ereport history is cleared after a complete scan, scrub_finish or resilver_finish is posted, and finished replacements are detached by the async thread.

wires.label: bio completion: vbio_completion() stores the device status in io_error (bi_status_to_errno()); a disk that returns wrong data completes without an error
zio_delay_interrupt() -> zio_interrupt(): queued on the interrupt taskq
an interrupt-taskq worker resumes the pipeline
leaf not accessible (dead, removal pending, or unable to read or write): io_error = ENXIO and zio_interrupt() without touching the disk
zio_vdev_io_done() -> zio_vdev_io_assess(): result of this vdev level
unexpected error on a leaf that still looks accessible and is not being removed: vdev_probe(vd, zio)
vdev_op_io_done(): vdev_disk_io_done()
EIO and zfs_check_disk_status() finds the block device gone: vdev_remove_wanted = TRUE, spa_async_request(SPA_ASYNC_REMOVE)
read: data arrived
this level is finished: success, or an error that is not retried here (a leaf error is never retried; it becomes ENXIO if the disk is no longer accessible)
logical zio (no vdev) failed and was not retried yet: ZIO_FLAG_IO_RETRY set, dispatched to the issue taskq
the retry runs VDEV_IO_START again, cutting in line (zio_requeue_io_start_cut_in_line)
zio_checksum_error() mismatch on a non-speculative read: vs_checksum_errors++ on the leaf
zfs_ereport_start_checksum(): a copy of the bad data is kept for the report
io_error = ECKSUM, passed up so another copy can be tried
child done: zio_notify_parent() lets the mirror continue
vdev_mirror_io_done(): no good copy yet -> vdev_mirror_child_select() picks the next child
zio_vdev_child_io(): read of the next child; once good data is in hand, repair writes (ZIO_FLAG_IO_REPAIR, ZIO_FLAG_SELF_HEAL) to the children that failed
vdev_raidz_io_done(): raidz_checksum_verify() fails, parity reconstruction finds the bad column
vdev_raidz_checksum_error(): vs_checksum_errors++ on the child disk of the bad column
zfs_ereport_post_checksum() with the reconstructed good data and the bad column data
repair write of the reconstructed column (ZIO_FLAG_IO_REPAIR, ZIO_FLAG_SELF_HEAL)
zio_done(): vdev_stat_update(); slow I/O on a live leaf: vs_slow_ios++; failed I/O (not ECKSUM) on a live leaf: vs_read_errors++ or vs_write_errors++ unless its ereport was a duplicate
failed I/O (not ECKSUM) on a leaf that is not dead: zfs_ereport_post(ereport.fs.zfs.io)
io_delay >= zio_slow_io_ms on a live leaf and the vdev's slow_io_events is on: zfs_ereport_post(ereport.fs.zfs.delay)
logical zio failed: zfs_ereport_post(ereport.fs.zfs.data) with the bookmark and no vdev
logical zio failed (EIO, or any error unless speculative or not propagated): spa_log_error(bookmark, birth txg) adds it to spa_errlist_last, or spa_errlist_scrub while a scrub runs
logical zio done: each pending report's zcr_finish() -> zfs_ereport_finish_checksum() with the good data, or with none if the read failed

root logical zio marked ZIO_POST_SUSPEND (a read or free that failed with ENXIO and failmode is not continue, an allocating write that failed with ENOSPC, or a must-succeed zio that cannot be re-executed): zio_suspend(ZIO_SUSPEND_IOERR)
allocating write failed (not ENOSPC, not CANFAIL): ZIO_POST_REEXECUTE; the root zio re-executes the whole tree on the claim issue taskq, indefinitely while it keeps failing

probe failed: zfs_ereport_post(ereport.fs.zfs.probe_failure)

SPA_ASYNC_RESILVER: dsl_scan_restart_resilver(), unless a rebuild is active or a resilver is running with resilver_defer enabled

zio_wait() still waiting after zfs_deadman_ziotime_ms: zio_deadman()
oldest active zio of a leaf older than the limit: zio_deadman() logs the tree and posts zfs_ereport_post(ereport.fs.zfs.deadman) for each leaf zio (every zio with zio_deadman_log_all)
zfs_deadman_failmode=continue: an active leaf zio with no children gets io_error = EINTR and zio_interrupt(); failmode panic: fm_panic()

refs.code: fm_panic("%s determined I/O to pool '%s' is hung.", tag, name);

wires.label: zfs_ereport_is_valid(), zfs_ereport_is_duplicate() and zfs_is_ratelimiting_event() passed: zfs_ereport_start()
fm_ereport_set() class and detector, payload; zfs_zevent_post(): inserted at the head, the oldest dropped at zfs_zevent_len_max

refs.code: fm_ereport_set(ereport, FM_EREPORT_VERSION, class, ena, detector, NULL);

wires.label: zfs_ereport_start_checksum() / zfs_ereport_post_checksum(): the same validity, duplicate and rate-limit checks (zfs_checksum_events_per_second)
checksum ereport built by zfs_ereport_start(): hung on io_logical->io_cksum_report (start) or annotated at once (post)
annotate_ecksum() adds bad ranges and bit counts (an empty result is dropped); zfs_zevent_post()

paths.title: Checksum error repaired
paths.summary: A disk returns wrong data without reporting an error. CHECKSUM_VERIFY (mirror) or the RAIDZ reconstruction finds the bad copy, counts it against the disk and prepares a checksum ereport, and redundancy supplies and rewrites good data. zed records the event in the disk's checksum SERD engine.
paths.ends: The caller got correct data, the disk's CKSUM count in zpool status is one higher, and the bad copy has been rewritten. By default ten such events within ten minutes degrade the disk (path cksum_degrade).

RAIDZ / dRAID top-level vdev: reconstruction identifies the bad column and the ereport is posted at once

paths.ends: The I/O succeeded. zpool status -s shows the SLOW count. With the SERD properties set the disk ends up DEGRADED as in path cksum_degrade; otherwise nothing changes.

paths.title: Hung I/O (deadman)
paths.summary: An I/O does not complete at all. Either spa_sync() runs for longer than zfs_deadman_synctime_ms, or a zio_wait() caller waits for longer than zfs_deadman_ziotime_ms. The deadman logs the hung zios and posts deadman ereports; zfs_deadman_failmode decides whether it also forces them to complete.
paths.ends: The deadman never faults a disk by itself. With failmode wait the I/O keeps waiting and the check repeats every zfs_deadman_checktime_ms; with continue the EINTR goes through normal error handling; with panic the system panics.

paths.title: Repeated I/O errors: zed faults the disk, a hot spare takes over
paths.summary: The io SERD engine of a disk fires (ten io ereports within ten minutes by default). After a 15 second grace period for a removal event, the diagnosis engine solves fault.fs.zfs.vdev.io, the retire agent faults the disk through libzfs, and a hot spare is attached as a replacement.
paths.ends: The disk is FAULTED (or DEGRADED if it held the only copy of some data) and no longer receives I/O. With a spare, a spare vdev holds the failed disk and the spare, and a resilver copies everything onto the spare; it continues in the scrub and resilver graph (`zfs-scrub-resilver:resilver`). The spare stays attached until the failed disk is replaced or brought back. A fault requested by zed is not kept when the pool is next imported; the disk is then opened again.

paths.ends: The disk is FAULTED without any SERD diagnosis. If a spare was attached, the resilver starts as in path zed_fault. When the only copy is affected the pool suspends instead (path suspend_clear, cause dead_disk).

paths.title: Device removed and returning (DTL, resilver)
paths.summary: A disk of a mirror disappears. It is marked REMOVED, earlier errors are forgiven, writes skip it and record their txgs in its DTL. When the disk is plugged back in, zed onlines it and a resilver copies exactly the missed txgs. A different blank disk in the same slot is used as a replacement when autoreplace is on.
paths.ends: A resilver starts that copies the txgs in the DTL to the returned disk (or everything to the new one); it continues in the scrub and resilver graph (`zfs-scrub-resilver:resilver`). After the administrator restores the devices, zpool clear clears the errors, reopens the devices and re-executes the held I/O.

paths.summary: A block cannot be read from any copy. The logical zio fails, its bookmark goes into the error log, which is written to the pool in the next txg, and zpool status -v lists the affected file. The entry goes away only when a later scrub completes without finding the error again.

paths.title: Where zpool status and zpool events get their data
paths.summary: zpool status reads the pool configuration with the per-vdev counters and the error count; zpool events reads the zevent queue through its own /dev/zfs cursor, exactly as zed does.
paths.ends: zpool status shows READ, WRITE and CKSUM (and SLOW with -s) per vdev from in-memory counters that start at zero at import and are reset by zpool clear; zpool events shows the events still in the queue (at most zfs_zevent_len_max).

steps.note: without -v only the approximate count

model: Errors are detected inside the zio pipeline when an I/O completes (VDEV_IO_DONE, VDEV_IO_ASSESS, CHECKSUM_VERIFY, DONE). Each problem is recorded in up to three separate places: an in-memory counter on the vdev (the READ, WRITE, CKSUM and SLOW columns of zpool status), an event in the kernel zevent queue, and, only when a logical read or write failed after all redundancy, an entry in the persistent error log.

The records are filtered. A disk that is already dead gets no counts and no ereports; an io or checksum ereport identical to one posted for the same disk within zfs_zevent_retain_expire_secs is a duplicate and dropped, and a duplicate io ereport does not raise the READ or WRITE counter either; checksum, delay and deadman ereports are rate limited per disk. The counters live only in memory and are reset by zpool clear.

The kernel does not fault a disk because of its error counts. zed reads the zevent queue through /dev/zfs; its diagnosis engine counts io and checksum ereports per disk in SERD engines (10 events in 600 seconds by default, tunable per vdev), and its retire agent then asks the kernel through libzfs to fault the disk (I/O errors) or degrade it (checksum errors, slow I/O) and to attach a hot spare. Without zed, a disk that keeps returning errors but still answers the kernel's probes stays ONLINE.

The kernel changes a disk's state on its own only when it cannot reach it: a failed probe of the label areas makes it FAULTED, a disk the operating system reports gone becomes REMOVED. If a disk to be faulted this way holds the only copy of some data, it is left DEGRADED and the pool suspends instead.

While a disk is missing, writes to it fail at once with ENXIO and their txgs are added to its dirty time log (DTL). When the disk comes back, or a spare or replacement is attached, a resilver copies exactly those txgs.

The pool suspends when I/O fails that must not be dropped: label writes in spa_sync(), a read of data whose every copy is on missing disks, or the only copy of some data being faulted. The failmode property decides what callers see meanwhile (wait, continue with EIO, or panic); zpool clear clears the errors, reopens the devices and re-executes every held I/O.

A permanent error is the bookmark of a logical block that could not be read or written. It is kept in memory, written to the pool's error log in the next txg, and listed by zpool status -v with file names resolved at that moment. zpool clear does not remove it; it disappears only when a scrub or resilver ends without having seen the error again (the code rotates the log at the end of every scan, completed or cancelled).
simplifications: The six zed read steps (zed_loop to libzfs_ev to the ioctl to the queue and back) are drawn for every event, although zed reads events continuously and processes them strictly one after the other.

The mirror and RAIDZ child zios go straight back to VDEV_IO_START in this graph; the I/O graph draws them through zio_vdev_child_io(). The logical zio, the top-level vdev zio and the leaf zios all pass through the same stage nodes.
Counters, ereports and DTL updates happen in the order of the code in zio_done(), but a path shows them in the order that reads best; several of them happen for each of the zios in a tree.

The SERD engines, cases and fault lists are zed's own small re-implementation of the illumos fault manager; there is no separate fmd process. Case state is not kept across zed restarts in the way illumos fmd keeps it.
Only the main event classes are named. Others (vdev.* open failures, config cache write failures, authentication, Direct I/O verify, log replay, pool load failures) follow the same ereport path.
Spare selection, dRAID spares and fault domains, multipath disks and partition handling in zfs_mod are reduced to one wire each.
The resilver itself, its DTL reassessment and the detach of a finished replacement or spare belong to the scrub and resilver graph.
MMP (multihost) suspends, which use the same suspend node, are not drawn.

page.title: ZFS Fault Management
page.intro: This diagram follows a misbehaving disk from the failed or wrong I/O in the zio pipeline to everything ZFS does about it: the per-vdev error counters shown by zpool status, the ereports and other events in the kernel zevent queue, the ZFS event daemon (zed) that reads them and decides whether a disk is faulted or degraded, the hot spare that replaces it, the dirty time log that remembers what a missing disk did not get, the pool suspend that stops I/O when nothing else is possible, and the persistent error log behind "permanent errors" in zpool status -v.
